/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Run a ParaView document (route schemaxis/1) as this operation. The paraview adaptor validates, plans and executes it exactly as a standalone document; later operations can use its verified artifacts and results through $artifact or the $value result form.

Run a Blender document (route schemaxis.blender/1) as this operation. The blender adaptor validates, plans and executes it exactly as a standalone document; later operations can use its verified artifacts and results through $artifact or the $value result form.

Run a FreeCAD document (route schemaxis.freecad/1) as this operation. The freecad adaptor validates, plans and executes it exactly as a standalone document; later operations can use its verified artifacts and results through $artifact or the $value result form.

Run a Blender production document (route schemaxis.blender.production/1) as this operation. Build an editable product scene from typed assets, shared materials, lighting, cameras, procedural node groups and motion; render checked frames and publish declared geometry formats. Its explicit import and export losses remain in force. Later operations can consume its verified publications through $artifact and its declared result fields through $value.

Run a FreeCAD assembly document (route schemaxis.freecad.assembly/1) as this operation: it assembles parts, unlike schemaxis.freecad/1, which models a single part. The freecad adaptor validates, plans and executes it as it would a standalone document; later operations can use its verified artifacts and results through $artifact or the $value result form.

Run a saved-scene render document (route schemaxis.blender.render/1) as this operation: it re-renders a .blend published by an earlier schemaxis.blender/1 operation from new cameras without rebuilding geometry, so it normally takes that .blend through $artifact. The blender adaptor validates, plans and executes it as it would a standalone document.

Run a FreeCAD technical sheet document (route schemaxis.freecad.drawing/1) as this operation. Create an editable TechDraw sheet from admitted frozen geometry, with standard views, measured dimensions, title information and SVG/PDF publication. The sheet does not automatically update from a later source revision. Later operations can consume its verified publications through $artifact and its declared result fields through $value.

Run a FreeCAD structural analysis document (route schemaxis.freecad.analysis/1) as this operation. Run the admitted linear-static solid FEM workflow with typed material, mesh, supports and loads, editable FEM objects and CalculiX results checked for equilibrium and energy. It does not cover every simulation family. Later operations can consume its verified publications through $artifact and its declared result fields through $value.

Run a Godot document (route schemaxis.godot/1) as this operation. The godot adaptor validates, plans and executes it exactly as a standalone document; later operations can use its verified artifacts and results through $artifact or the $value result form. Timed sprites use both a captured sheet image and its supported frame/tag metadata; the editable resource and headless playback checks do not certify rendering or real-time pacing.

Run an Aseprite document (route schemaxis.aseprite/1) as this operation. The aseprite adaptor validates, plans and executes it as it would a standalone document; later operations can use its verified artifacts and results through $artifact or the $value result form.

Prepare bounded three-axis face milling and closed flat-floor pockets from a verified retained CAD solid (route schemaxis.freecad.cam/1). Declare a reachable straight endmill, pre-sized blank and clamping base. Native toolpaths, LinuxCNC code and independently checked remaining/gouged material are required before publication; profiling, general holding strategies and broader CAM remain unfinished.

Evaluate prescribed rigid mechanical motion and interference over an authored finite timeline (route schemaxis.freecad.mechanism/1). Named bodies and joint frames remain editable in the saved native assembly; geometric invariants and fresh reopen checks verify the result. This evaluates declared kinematics rather than predicting forces or simulating contact dynamics.

Run a GNU Octave document (route schemaxis.octave/1) as this operation. The octave adaptor validates, plans and executes it exactly as a standalone document; later operations can use its verified artifacts and results through $artifact or the $value result form.

Publish declared numeric or typed labelled tables as checked editable Calc workbooks. Captured CSV requires an explicit header/type/null contract; a file artifact alone does not prove compatible table contents. Numeric summaries use only numeric columns, and empty text is excluded from the typed path (route schemaxis.calc/1).

Prepare an explicitly typed nullable table with declared row selection and column mappings, publishing independently checked Parquet and a report. An explicit option adds typed CSV for a downstream consumer that declares a compatible schema; the CSV itself carries no type or unit metadata (route schemaxis.apachearrow/1).
pitfalls: Declare every source column type and nullability; empty text is distinct from the reserved \N null token.
Only int32-to-int64 widening and explicit null replacement are supported. The fixed Parquet publication is a file artifact; no generic downstream Parquet import or metadata preservation is promised.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Run a CalculiX document (route schemaxis.calculix/1) as this operation. The calculix adaptor validates, plans and executes it exactly as a standalone document; later operations can use its verified artifacts and results through $artifact or the $value result form.

Run a Cantera document (route schemaxis.cantera/1) as this operation. The cantera adaptor validates, plans and executes it exactly as a standalone document; later operations can use its verified artifacts and results through $artifact or the $value result form.

Run an Elmer steady one-dimensional solid-conduction stack as this operation: declare material layers, uniform heat sources, value, outward-flux or convection ends and sampled limits. Native saved-field reopening, independent exact conduction and source-corrected balances support verified publications for later operations through $artifact or the $value result form. (route schemaxis.elmer/1).
pitfalls: This route excludes fluid flow, transient or coupled physics and general geometry. Limits apply to the stated mesh samples; native ASCII VTU has eight significant digits while the restart-backed tables retain full precision.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Check a finished EPUB with the configured EPUBCheck launcher (route schemaxis.epubcheck/1). The operation captures its bytes, checks the supported package structure, and publishes an assessment only when fresh standards checks agree and report zero fatal findings, errors and warnings. A Pandoc EPUB artifact can pass directly into this step.
pitfalls: The fixed zero-warning policy can refuse an EPUB that a reading application opens. Check the named findings before handing over the publication.
Standards-check results have a bounded scope; accessibility, reading-system behaviour and content security need their own assessment.
The checker uses a fixed offline policy and a trusted configured launcher. That policy is separate from an operating-system network sandbox.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Create an offline synthetic narration draft from a literal script or a verified plain-text artifact (route schemaxis.espeakng/1). Choose a requested US English (default), British English, French or Spanish voice. The script stays unchanged; selecting a voice does not translate it. Output is PCM16 mono 22050 Hz WAV for downstream SoX preparation or FLAC archiving. A bounded speaking rate is also authored; no audio playback or speech recognition runs.
pitfalls: A transcript artifact supplies text, not evidence that a person reviewed it. Listen to the synthetic output before publishing; pronunciation, intelligibility and accessibility are not certified.
Execution and verification need a trusted eSpeak NG 1.52.0 installation with matching native data. Native objects and voice handles never cross workflow boundaries.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Read, audit or compare photo metadata with ExifTool as this operation (route schemaxis.exiftool/1): inventoryPhotos (fixed selected fields of 1 to 16 baseline JPEGs) or inspectMetadata, auditMetadata and compareMetadata over a media set of JPEG photos and XMP sidecars. Typed CSV artifacts (inventory.csv at artifact index 1 for inventoryPhotos; the profile-<name>.csv, findings.csv or differences.csv tables after metadata.json and manifest.json for the workbench operations) can feed a Calc readTypedCSV node for an editable workbook. Results are observed metadata, not certified capture time, location, authorship or privacy.
pitfalls: Select the table artifact by its index: inventoryPhotos publishes metadata.json (0) and inventory.csv (1); inspectMetadata publishes metadata.json (0), manifest.json (1) and then one profile CSV per requested profile in the authored profile order of the catalogue; audit and compare publish their JSON then CSV after the manifest.
A Calc handoff needs a CSV with at least one row and at least two present values in every number column; choose a profile the photos actually record.
Changing a photo's bytes at the same path, or adding or removing a file in a scanned folder, re-runs this step and every consumer; unchanged inputs reuse them.
Verifying a run that requested the native listing needs a configured trusted ExifTool to replay it.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Run a bounded FFmpeg document (route schemaxis.ffmpeg/1) as this operation: publish ordered PNG frames or sprite sheets as video, select a frame range from an existing silent video, combine FFV1 video/PCM16 audio/SubRip captions as a review movie, extract an explicit AAC-LC stream from MP4/M4A into canonical PCM16 WAV, or encode a captured PCM16 WAV as AAC-LC M4A. Audio extraction can feed SoX conform before transcription; encodeAudio can publish verified narration or a prepared WAV. Every publication needs a fresh trusted native decode during verification; captions and audio remain draft or author-declared review, with no recognition or perceptual certification.
pitfalls: AAC extraction decodes an already lossy source; it cannot recover the original recording. Select the global audio stream index explicitly.

encodeAudio is lossy. Author maxBytes and maxMeanPCMError explicitly; the error budget is measured in signed PCM16 sample units and is not a listening-quality preset. Bitrate is an encoder target, not an exact output-size promise.
WAV publication supports the declared bounded sample rates, mono or stereo, at most 600 seconds and 32 MiB of captured source. It does not resample, mix channels or normalise volume.
Keep the captured inputs and trusted FFmpeg with sibling ffprobe available for fresh verification. Recorded executable paths are provenance consistency checks, never a source of executable authority.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Archive bounded PCM16 WAV as lossless FLAC, or decode a captured native FLAC to PCM16 WAV for audio preparation (route schemaxis.flac/1). Both operations compare exact PCM using a trusted fresh native decoder; decoded WAV can feed SoX conform before transcription.
pitfalls: Mono/stereo PCM16 only; no Ogg FLAC, 24-bit conversion, mixing or resampling. Metadata tags are not carried into the decoded WAV.
FLAC verification needs the trusted configured decoder. Exact PCM consistency against writable captures does not authenticate the original recording or its producer.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Run a GDAL raster window document (route schemaxis.gdal/1) as this operation: capture a supported north-up single-band GeoTIFF, select a pixel window and optionally resize its grid by nearest-neighbour sampling. Explicit source CRS, band units and nodata assertions must match the captured metadata. Publish a georeferenced raster and numeric summary checked by an independent TIFF reader and a fresh native reopen.
pitfalls: Resizing preserves the selected outer extent but discards or repeats samples; it does not conserve integrals.
This route does not reproject. EPSG4326 horizontal coordinates are degrees, while EPSG3857 coordinates are metres; band units are separate.
A downstream raster window addresses the producer output grid, not the original input pixels.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Run a GetDP layered scalar-conduction document (route schemaxis.getdp/1) as this operation: solve steady one-dimensional heat or electric-current conduction with material layers, sources, end conditions and sampled limits. Generated native files, independent continuum solutions and conservation checks support verified artifacts and results for later operations through $artifact or the $value result form.
pitfalls: This route does not accept general geometry, transient/vector fields or arbitrary GetDP programs. An optional downstream application must be qualified separately.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Run a Gmsh document (route schemaxis.gmsh/1) as this operation. The gmsh adaptor validates, plans and executes it exactly as a standalone document; later operations can use its verified artifacts and results through $artifact or the $value result form.

Run a Gnuplot plot document (route schemaxis.gnuplot/1) as this operation: draw one to four declared numeric CSV series with explicit units, linear or logarithmic axes, and either optional symmetric y errors or an asserted asymmetric lower/upper range envelope (series bounds: shaded piecewise-linear display of supplied bounds; no quantile, confidence level or coverage is computed; linear axes, one series). Publish independently checked SVG and PNG plus the captured table and editable plot script. A verified CSV artifact of kind table or file (for example an Apache Arrow publishCSV table.csv, artifact index 2) can supply the data; its bytes are captured and parsed with the same closed numeric-CSV rules before Gnuplot starts, and the column units are asserted by the Gnuplot document, not carried by the CSV; authored scripts and general Gnuplot commands are outside this route.
pitfalls: Declare columns in the exact header order of the CSV artifact; a wrong header, missing cell, non-numeric or binary file is refused before Gnuplot starts.
Use error for a symmetric absolute interval and bounds for an asserted lower/upper range; they cannot be combined, and the envelope never computes uncertainty.
Select the CSV by artifact index (Apache Arrow publishCSV: index 2); an operation that did not publish a CSV leaves that index absent.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Run a Graphviz layout document (route schemaxis.graphviz/1) as this operation: declare named directed nodes and edges, choose top-to-bottom or left-to-right layout, and require an acyclic graph or explicitly allow cycles. Publish trusted editable DOT, SVG and checked layout geometry; topology, labels, box separation and edge attachment are verified.
pitfalls: Automatic layout does not promise the fewest crossings or optimal placement.
Plain and SVG share the native layout engine; their consistency is checked separately from independent declared topology invariants.
No authored DOT, HTML labels, external images, clusters or arbitrary native attributes are exposed.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Build, adopt, inspect, edit, compare or extract typed HDF5 scientific files with hierarchical datasets, units, dimension scales, selected storage and explicit dependent files (route schemaxis.hdf5/1). Mesh and field series publish XDMF companions; Typed row predicates, storage audits and fixed-size memory-bounded extraction compose with edits and received human-readable object names; bounded SWMR and local MPI read/write variants have separate native requirements. Immutable captured inputs and independent native readers govern handoffs. Broader application-wide acceptance remains open.

Schedule the plain IfcWall occurrences of one small ASCII IFC4 file with IfcOpenShell as this operation (route schemaxis.ifcopenshell/1): a GUID-linked typed table of the property and quantity columns you name, with the origin of every cell and project SI units converted to metres, square metres or cubic metres. It takes no upstream artifact; its typed CSV table can be bound by a Calc readTypedCSV step, so a changed property, quantity or unit prefix at the same IFC path re-runs both steps. The schedule reports stated values for coordination review, not geometry, model certification or quantity accuracy.
pitfalls: Declare the Calc columns exactly as published (GUID, Name, then your columns) with null token \N; each numeric column needs at least two present values there.
A missing value is null, never zero; choose missing and inheritance policies explicitly.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Run an ImageJ document (route schemaxis.imagej/1): threshold one calibrated grayscale image for particle measurements, or measure named rectangular regions across declared grayscale frames. Keep calibration, frame identities, times and the measurement policy explicit. A verified region-measurements.csv can feed Calc readTypedCSV with explicit text/numeric columns; particle tables retain their numeric handoff.
pitfalls: Rectangular regions and frame times are authored assumptions, not tracked objects, image registration or independently established acquisition metadata.
A captured CSV artifact must satisfy the consumer header, type and missing-value contract; artifact kind alone does not establish compatibility.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Run an ImageMagick raster document (route schemaxis.imagemagick/1) as this operation: crop captured RGB/RGBA8 PNGs, magnify by integer nearest-neighbour replication, apply clockwise quarter turns and preserve alpha or flatten encoded sRGB samples onto a declared background. An optional row-major comparison sheet publishes a JSON tile index. Verified image artifacts can feed later operations; colour assumptions and pixel budgets remain explicit.
pitfalls: Untagged input needs the explicit assume-srgb policy; this is a recorded interpretation, not colour conversion.
No arbitrary ImageMagick options, external delegates, font labels or general format conversion are exposed.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Bundle 1 to 16 selected publication files under chosen flat ASCII names using Info-ZIP (route schemaxis.infozip/1). Captured files are stored without compression in a ZIP with an explicit inventory; verification checks every payload byte, its name and its inventory entry. This provides one delivery artifact for audio, captions, text and other selected outputs.
pitfalls: The selection is bounded to 32 MiB per file and 64 MiB in total, with a closed set of filename extensions. ZIP headers and the inventory add a small overhead.
File bytes remain unchanged, including content metadata. The bundle inventory verifies byte agreement rather than media quality, file-format validity or signed origin.
Use case preservation when the handoff also needs the authored workflow, receipts and other case evidence.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Run an Inkscape document (route schemaxis.inkscape/1) as this operation. The inkscape adaptor validates, plans and executes it as it would a standalone document; later operations can use its verified artifacts and results through $artifact or the $value result form.

Run a KiCad document (route schemaxis.kicad/1) as this operation: inspect an existing two-layer board, gate its native DRC findings or export checked Excellon drills. Failed DRC limits block downstream publication. This route does not author boards or translate them into an ngspice circuit.
pitfalls: Coordinate units do not determine the units of scalar/vector data arrays; those values are retained without automatic conversion.
The supported ASCII subset excludes solver formats, binary/compressed payloads, unsupported topology and metadata.
This is interchange with bounded orientation checks, not mesh repair or remeshing.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Run a meshio conversion document (route schemaxis.meshio/1) as this operation: capture a supported ASCII VTU or legacy VTK mesh and explicitly declare source and target length units. Preserve ordered triangle/tetra/eight-node-hexahedron connectivity and numeric point/cell arrays while converting coordinates. Independent readers check retained source and output; unsupported data is refused by the strict loss policy.
pitfalls: Hexahedral signed volumes and positive sampled Jacobians do not prove global cell validity. Field values and associations are preserved; only coordinate units are transformed.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Run a MuPDF review document (route schemaxis.mupdf/1) as this operation: capture an unencrypted PDF, select pages in explicit order, and publish page PNGs, extracted text and crop/rotation metadata. DPI controls raster geometry and native font mappings determine text extraction. This passive review does not certify reading order, sanitize the PDF or preserve editable document features.

Run a ngspice document (route schemaxis.ngspice/1) as this operation. The ngspice adaptor validates, plans and executes it exactly as a standalone document; later operations can use its verified artifacts and results through $artifact or the $value result form.
pitfalls: STL carries no physical units; later consumers must explicitly select millimetres.
Circular walls are inscribed polygons. Nominal across-vertices diameter differs from across-flats clearance.
Geometry verification does not certify mechanical strength, manufacturability or printer suitability.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Run a NumPy measurement-table document (route schemaxis.numpy/1) as this operation: capture labelled numeric channels, centre and scale them explicitly, and compute principal components. Publish independently checked spectrum, reconstruction and either separated component loadings/scores or a retained-subspace projector. Host-owned met, unmet and indeterminate requirements determine whether later operations may consume the results.
pitfalls: Different channel units require declared scaling or standardisation.
Repeated or nearly repeated components do not have stable individual directions; use the subspace contract.
Numerical agreement does not establish physical meaning or statistical significance.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Run an OpenSCAD dimensioned part document (route schemaxis.openscad/1) as this operation: construct a mounting plate with separated through-holes or an annular spacer from explicit millimetre dimensions. Publish a verified binary STL, generated native SCAD and measured summary. Independent contour, orientation, topology and faceted-volume checks constrain the supported parts.
pitfalls: STL carries no physical units; later consumers must explicitly select millimetres.
Circular walls are inscribed polygons. Nominal across-vertices diameter differs from across-flats clearance.
Geometry verification does not certify mechanical strength, manufacturability or printer suitability.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Run a bounded OpenSees planar elastic truss analysis as this operation: declare nodes, pin-jointed members, zero-translation supports, loads and measured serviceability limits. Independent stiffness and equilibrium checks support the signed member-force, stress, reaction and displacement publications. Verified artifacts and results can feed later operations through $artifact or the $value result form. (route schemaxis.opensees/1).
pitfalls: This route excludes frames, bending, buckling, nonlinear materials, dynamics and general earthquake engineering. Fresh process reconstruction is distinct from native database persistence.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Run an Oracle typed database document (route schemaxis.oracle/1) as this operation: inspect a schema, load declared typed tables, report over relational/document values or execute a checked atomic mutation with an idempotency ledger. The isolated driver, independent reference and retained outcome evidence support later operations through $artifact or the $value result form. Credentials remain in the named environment variables.
pitfalls: A committed or unknown database outcome must be inspected before retrying; workflow resume does not undo database effects. Existing-table mutations refuse undeclared trigger/cascade effects and this route accepts no arbitrary SQL or PL/SQL.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Run a Pandoc report document (route schemaxis.pandoc/1) as this operation: publish the same declared headings, paragraphs, tables and captured PNG figures as HTML and DOCX (with an optional bounded EPUB 3 package), then independently check their content and image geometry. Figures can come from compatible verified workflow artifacts. This route accepts the bounded report structure, not arbitrary markup, styles, templates or filters.
pitfalls: An EPUB package/content check does not certify EPUBCheck conformance, reading-device rendering or accessibility.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Run a PrusaSlicer document (route schemaxis.prusaslicer/1) as this operation: slice one closed STL using declared units and printer, material and print settings, then verify the emitted G-code within the documented limits. The output is a file for review; the route never connects to or controls a printer.

Run a pyproj route-chainage document (route schemaxis.pyproj/1) as this operation: capture ordered WGS84 longitude/latitude waypoints and place labelled stations at ellipsoidal distances continuously across turning points. Publish independently checked station/leg tables and GeoJSON. Host-owned numerical bands decide declared length and closure requirements; unmet or indeterminate results block downstream operations.
pitfalls: This route performs no datum, CRS, height or epoch transformation and does not certify survey accuracy.
Coordinate order is longitude then latitude; limits on latitude, leg length and antimeridian crossings are explicit.
GeoJSON connects sampled stations with straight coordinate segments, not native geodesic curves.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Run a QGIS document (route schemaxis.qgis/1) as this operation. The qgis adaptor validates, plans and executes it exactly as a standalone document; later operations can use its verified artifacts and results through $artifact or the $value result form.

Run a QPDF page assembly document (route schemaxis.qpdf/1) as this operation: capture bounded PDF sources, select pages in explicit order with repetitions and relative clockwise quarter turns, then publish a new PDF with recorded document-level losses. Fresh QPDF and MuPDF processes check the actual output against captured pages; verification is bounded to structural checks and exact 36 dpi raster, text and geometry observations. Later operations can consume the verified PDF through $artifact.
pitfalls: This route is not a PDF sanitiser or a proof of equivalence in every reader or at every resolution.
Labels and document metadata are discarded; selected-page annotations, forms, signatures, encryption and other unsupported features are refused.
Ordinary saved verification requires trusted QPDF and MuPDF runtimes.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Run an R document (route schemaxis.r/1) as this operation. The r adaptor validates, plans and executes it as it would a standalone document; later operations can use its verified artifacts and results through $artifact or the $value result form. Explicit predictor-only new rows can request mean-response confidence or individual future-observation prediction intervals. These meanings differ, and both rely on the declared OLS assumptions; neither proves model validity. A compatible table consumer can use the published prediction.csv.

Edit a bounded silent-video timeline with Shotcut (route schemaxis.shotcut/1). Named captured assets and ordered frame ranges form one contiguous timeline. The outputs are a rendered video, an editable MLT project and a bundle containing the project with its captured media. Verification reloads the native project, compares the complete original and reloaded renders, and checks every selected source frame within the stated colour-conversion limits.
pitfalls: Inputs must have matching integer frame rates and dimensions, progressive square pixels and no audio or subtitles; resizing, frame-rate conversion, transitions and multiple tracks are unsupported.
Keep the captured media beside project.mlt when relocating the editable project, or use the checked project bundle; the project alone does not contain its media.
Frame checks permit bounded MLT colour conversion; they do not certify perceptual quality, colour management or GUI editing.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Choose a bounded SoX recording operation (route schemaxis.sox/1). Assemble cuts PCM16 clips by sample frame, applies declared gains and fades, then concatenates them. Conform prepares one recording as mono 16 kHz for transcription under a declared channel policy. Normalise keeps rate, channels and frames while scaling every channel by one measured gain to a declared PCM16 sample peak. Assembly and normalisation check every output sample; resampling uses the stated band-limited projection checks.
pitfalls: In assemble, gain is a linear amplitude multiplier, not decibels. Potential clipping before fades is refused.
In assemble, frames contain one sample per channel. The last stored fade-out frame retains 1/N gain; its zero endpoint lies just after the clip.
normalise controls sample peak, not loudness or true peak. Boosting amplifies noise with the signal; maxGain is an explicit policy ceiling, and excessive gain is refused.
Conform resampling is lossy and verifies only the declared projection band and interior samples. Keep the original recording when its full bandwidth matters.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Run a SQLite summary document (route schemaxis.sqlite/1) as this operation: import captured typed JSON tables into a fresh database, enforce declared primary and foreign keys, then filter, join and group them to publish exact integer totals, counts, JSON and CSV. Null and empty text stay distinct. Only the closed relational operations are available; authored SQL and existing database mutation are excluded.

Run a SymPy real-root isolation document (route schemaxis.sympy/1) as this operation: isolate every real root of one polynomial with exact rational coefficients into disjoint rational intervals, retaining multiplicities. An independent host Sturm check certifies the published root list. Coefficients are literal fraction strings with no expression syntax; only the declared bounded polynomial contract is supported.
pitfalls: The coefficient values are exact inputs; root certification does not establish that an upstream physical or fitted model is valid.
Only real roots are published. Complex roots are counted with multiplicity but are not isolated.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Recognize the text of one scanned-page PNG with Tesseract and a pinned English model as this operation (route schemaxis.tesseract/1). The image can be a verified image artifact of an earlier step, such as a rendered PDF page; the result is a machine-draft text, word boxes and summary for human review, not certified text or a page identity.
pitfalls: Confidence is uncalibrated; review the draft against the page image.

Pick pageSegmentation to match the layout. A mismatch can return no words or wrong text; no text was observed for single-line on the two-line qualification fixture, and OCR_NO_TEXT is not a reliable detector of a wrong choice.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Run a WebP image document (route schemaxis.webp/1) as this operation: encode a bounded PNG as exact lossless WebP or opaque lossy WebP within explicit error and byte budgets, or decode a supported static WebP into canonical PNG for reuse by PNG-only consumers. Verification decodes held bytes again with trusted native dwebp; it proves agreement with that decoder, not an independent WebP implementation or perceptual quality.
pitfalls: The encode operations need cwebp and dwebp; decodeToPng needs only dwebp; verification needs a trusted configured dwebp.
encodeLossless does not preserve PNG metadata or colour profiles. Animation, extended (VP8X) WebP files and other image formats are outside this route.
decodeToPng restores the samples of the WebP decoder, not the pixels discarded by lossy encoding. Metadata is dropped; producer and consumer byte/dimension budgets must both be met.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Lay out captions from one SHA-256-pinned machine or author-reviewed timed-text document (route schemaxis.whispercpp.captions/1). Choose 8 to 80 Unicode code points per line and 1 to 3 lines per cue. The host selects balanced breaks at isolated ordinary spaces while preserving every source character, cue and millisecond time, then publishes SubRip, WebVTT and a layout summary.
pitfalls: A run of adjacent spaces stays together, and text without suitable break points can exceed the chosen width and be refused. Cue words and times remain unchanged.
Code-point length differs from displayed width and readability. The source review status is carried as its author declared it; a person still needs to assess captions against the recording.
A changed source requires a newly reviewed SHA-256 pin; stale bytes are refused rather than laid out silently.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Apply a pinned human correction declaration to an existing draft transcript (route schemaxis.whispercpp.correct/1). The host preserves cue timing and publishes corrected text, captions and a provenance ledger without running ASR or loading a model.
pitfalls: Review status is an author declaration, not proof of a person reviewing the recording or recognition accuracy.
Use two phases: retain and review a draft, then pin its known digest in the correction document. An automatic transcription-to-correction workflow cannot supply an informed human review declaration.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Apply an explicit, pinned correction declaration with cue deletion to a completed machine draft (route schemaxis.whispercpp.correct/2). Replacement and deletion indices refer to the original cues; the publication renumbers the retained cues and records the source mapping and deletion ledger. This host-only step loads no model and runs no speech recognition.
pitfalls: Pin the reviewed draft bytes before authoring this second phase; the workflow cannot infer a human decision to delete a cue. Status and notes are author declarations, not proof of a person reviewing the recording.

Deleting every cue produces empty plain text and SubRip plus a WebVTT header. Pandoc publishes explicit no-retained-cues provenance without a cue table; captionReview is refused for this empty result.

Retain the original draft path for workflow verification. Job-only verification replays the captured draft; neither path authenticates an original recording against a coherent rewrite of writable captures.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Apply an explicit, pinned correction declaration with author-edited cue times to a completed machine draft (route schemaxis.whispercpp.correct/3). Replacement, deletion and timing indices refer to the original cues; each timing edit states the whole new start and end as integer milliseconds, and the publication renumbers the retained cues, records the original and edited time of every retimed cue and says the times are the author's declaration. The host never runs ASR, listens to the audio or changes the audio.
pitfalls: Pin the reviewed draft bytes before authoring this second phase; the workflow cannot infer a human decision about timing. Status, note and edited times are author declarations, not proof of a person reviewing the recording or of audio synchronization.
The finished cues must be ordered, nonoverlapping and inside the audio duration; a violation is refused naming the offending edit and is never clamped, reordered or rounded.

Retain the original draft path for workflow verification. Job-only verification replays the captured draft; neither path authenticates an original recording against a coherent rewrite of writable captures.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Run a whisper.cpp transcription document (route schemaxis.whispercpp/1) as this operation: capture a local PCM16 mono 16000 Hz WAV, use an explicitly selected SHA-256-pinned local model, and publish draft text, millisecond segment data, SRT and WebVTT captions. The native process stays offline; independent checks validate timing and agreement between retained segment evidence and the files. An optional word-aware segment-length target uses experimental native token timing; it does not guarantee a maximum cue length.
pitfalls: A verified transcription is structurally consistent evidence, not certified recognition accuracy. Review the words and caption suitability against the audio before publishing.

SoX conform preserves the recording time axis within final-frame rounding. After assemble cuts or concatenation, transcript times refer to the edited WAV; use its checked segment map to relate them to original source frames.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Run an xarray named-coordinate profile document (route schemaxis.xarray/1) as this operation: capture one local classic NetCDF CDF-1 measurement cube, assert its variable, dimension names, order and units, select inclusive numeric coordinate ranges, average the other dimensions with an explicit missing policy and publish a smaller NetCDF profile, a numeric profile.csv and a hashed summary. Isolated xarray does the reduction offline in its own process; an independent standard-library reader checks every coordinate, value, unit and count.
pitfalls: The mean is an unweighted arithmetic mean of the selected cells, not area, volume or time weighted, and carries no uncertainty claim. Declared dimensions must list the file's storage order.

To plot the profile, give a Gnuplot operation source {"$artifact": "<id>", "index": 1} (profile.csv) and declare its four columns and units yourself; a propagate profile with an empty mean cell is refused by Gnuplot.

/properties/operations/items/properties/.explanation: Compress or restore captured bytes and named directory selections, train or inspect reusable dictionaries, encode a change against an earlier snapshot, join checked frames, compare compressed sizes or measure native throughput (route schemaxis.zstandard/1). Workflows may consume pinned adopted files and complete directory snapshots. Exact content, captured dependencies and current frame controls are verified before handoff. This preserves file content rather than filesystem ownership or timestamps; historical benchmark timings and adaptive level schedules remain observational.
